ProductionConsumptionSettlement.title: Production and Consumption - Settlement
ProductionConsumptionSettlement.description: Production and consumption based on settlement data from Datahub. Data from 2005, but please note additional info in comments.
ProductionConsumptionSettlement.comment:
Data is updated with a 9-15 day delay.

Measurement data may be updated up to 2 years after the specific date, however data is normally 99% correct after 15 days, and will gradually be improved with the last update after 3 months. After 3 months, data will normally be 99,9% correct.

Data from 2005, but not in all rows:
* Commercial power separated from local power from 2021.
* Solar power divided into the four columns from 2020. Before 2020 all solar power is placed in SolarPowerSelfConMWh.
* Transmission grid loss from 1/10 2008. Zero is actually a null.
* GridLossDistributionMWh and GridLossInterconnectorsMWh from 1/1 2021.
* In some cases, zero should actually be a null.

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=now-P15D](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/ProductionConsumptionSettlement?start=now-P15D) is a good approach. Making a request once daily after 8:30 CET is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.\
Since data may be updated up to 6 months retrospectively, it is recommended to request a larger volume of data once each month to ensure accurate results.
ProductionConsumptionSettlement.author: Energinet

columns.description: Electricity production from central thermal power plants.
columns.comment:
Electricity production from Central Power Plants per municipality per month. Central Power Plants are defined as being located at the following production facility locations: Amagerværket, Asnæsværket, Avedøreværket, H. C. Ørstedsværket, Kyndbyværket, Svanemølleværket, Stigsnæsvær-ket, Rønneværket, Enstedværket, Esbjergværket, Fynsværket, Herningværket, Randersværket, Skærbækværket, Studstrupvæket and Nordjyllandsværket. Or at any other production plant locations, where the capacity is above 100 MW.
Please see the legal notice [Kraftværksbekendtgørelsen Kapitel 6, § 17](https://www.retsinformation.dk/Forms/R0710.aspx?id=163522) (Danish).

columns.description: Sum of production from local Combined Heat and Power units (CHP).
columns.comment: Include all thermal power plants with the single purpose to deliver power to the grid (except for central power plant). Nearly all local power is combined heat and power, except power plants running on bio-gas.

columns.description: Commercial power plant not only operates to deliver power to grid, but mainly serve other purposes. This could be waste incineration or any other process, where the electricity production could be considered as a bi-product.
Production from commercial power plants, that is not delivered to the grid. Named before commercial power was separated from Local power, therefor the confusing DB name.
columns.comment: Very uncertain, as values depends on metering point setup, and self-consumption is not required in Datahub. The "real" self-consumption is published yearly in the national declaration on Energinets homepage.

columns.description: Production from Offshore wind power plants with an installed capacity under 100 MW.
Production from Offshore wind power plants with an installed capacity greater or equal to 100 MW.
Production from onshore wind power generators with an installed capacity under 50 kW.
Production from onshore wind power generators with an installed capacity greater or equal to 50 kW.
Production from Hydro power.
columns.comment: In some historical data, hydro power included in "Local Power".

columns.description: Production from solar panels with an installed capacity below 10 kW.
Production from solar panels with an installed capacity between 10 and 40 kW (10 kW included).
Production from solar panels with an installed capacity greater than, or equal to 40 kW.

The estimated production from solar panels, which has been consumed rather than released to the grid. The value is the difference between the modelled (expected) production and the actual production from solar panels. When the modelled value is smaller than the actual value, the local power self-consumption is set to zero.
columns.comment: The estimated production is based on real-time measurements, occasionally containing small errors that are not corrected retroactively. Consequently, these estimates may deviate from actual production, such as instances of minimal nighttime solar panel output.

columns.description: Production without technology information.
columns.comment: Usually caused by missing links to structural data in "Stamdataregisteret".

columns.description: Exchange of Energy to Norway. Negative values are Export, positive values are import.
Exchange of Energy to Sweden. Negative values are export, positive values are import.
Exchange of Energy to Germany. Negative values are Export, positive values are import.
Exchange of Energy to the Netherlands. Negative values are Export, positive values are import.
Exchange of Energy to Great Britain. Negative values are Export, positive values are import.
Exchange of Energy over the Great Belt connection. Negative values are Export, positive values are import.

The total Gross consumption including losses in the electricity grid. Calculated as sum of all production including self-consumption plus sum of exchange. 

**Note**: Includes "*Commercial power self-consumption*", and therefor higher than in the dataset "Generation per Production Type and Exchange". However, "*Commercial power self-consumption*" is very uncertain, and overlaps *"Solar Power Self Consumption"*, and therefor to be excluded i the total consumption.
columns.comment:
* Total consumption through the grid is GrossConsumptionMWh - SolarPowerSelfConMWh - LocalPowerSelfConMWh
* Net consumption is GrossConsumptionMWh - GridLossTransmissionMWh - GridLossDistributionMWh

Gross consumption is measured from the connection point internally in DK, so GridLossInterconnectorsMWh is not included.

columns.description: Internal Losses in the transmission grid.
columns.comment: Do not include interconnectors, but includes the Great belt connection.

columns.description: Grid losses on interconnectors.
columns.comment: Not included in the Gross consumption.

columns.description: Losses in the distribution grid.
Conversion of Electricity to heat, often in district heating systems. Please read comments
columns.comment:
Includes both electric boilers and large heat pumps. 
More master data on "power to heat" units has been compiled spring 2026, and data has been updated back in time. 
Note, the consumption is already included in Gross consumption, and should not be added. 
Only include what is delivered from the grid, not any self consumption.

DayAheadPrices.title: Day-Ahead Prices
DayAheadPrices.description:
Day-Ahead Prices for Denmark and Neighboring Countries.

This dataset provides day-ahead electricity prices for Denmark (DK1 and DK2) and neighboring countries in the Nord Pool market, including Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Germany. In the day-ahead market, participants buy and sell electricity for delivery the following day within their respective bidding zones.
DayAheadPrices.comment:
The day-ahead prices reflect the balance between supply and demand and serve as a key indicator of market dynamics across the Nordic and European power systems.

The Day-Ahead Price (DKK) is calculated based on the Day-Ahead Price (EUR) and the Euro exchange rate from Danmarks Nationalbank. It may therefore deviate from Danish Day-Ahead prices seen elsewhere.

For data before 2025-10-01 see [Elspot Prices](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/Elspotprices) (hourly resolution).

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the Day-Ahead Prices for tomorrow, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=StartOfDay%2BP1D](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/DayAheadPrices?start=StartOfDay%2BP1D) is a good approach. Making a request every five minutes or so between 13:00 and 14:00 CET is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
DayAheadPrices.author: Energinet

Elspotprices.title: Elspot Prices (Discontinued – see description)
Elspotprices.description:
This dataset is no longer updated. For data after 2025-09-30 see [Day-Ahead Prices](https://energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/DayAheadPrices).

---

Day ahead spotprices in Denmark (DK) and neighbouring countries.
Elspotprices.comment:
From February 1st, 2025, the Spot Price (DKK) is calculated based on the Spot Price (EUR) and the Euro exchange rate from Danmarks Nationalbank. It may therefore deviate from Danish spot prices seen elsewhere.

From February 7th, 2025, the SYSTEM price is no longer available.

In Nord Pool Spot market players can buy and sell electricity for delivery the following day in their own area - Norway, Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Germany. The day-ahead prices indicate the balance between supply and demand.
Elspotprices.author: Energinet

ImbalancePrice.title: Imbalance Price
ImbalancePrice.description: This dataset shows all relevant information regarding the imbalance price design. The data is in 15-minute resolution and shows satisfied demand and the imbalance price and contains all the components relevant to the imbalance price, including the aFRR volumes, aFRR volume-weighted average price, and the mFRR marginal price.
ImbalancePrice.comment:
**Note**: The data will always reflect the prevailing conditions in the market design. Before March 4th, 2026 the dominating direction was determined by Balancing demand. From March 4th, 2026 the dominating direction is determined by Satisfied demand. Before March 19th, 2025 the imbalance price equal imbalance price from Pricing Module.  

Balancing demand (mFRR SA), can not be found in a new dynamic dataset mFRR Energy Activation Market.

**Find more** information about imbalance price design here: [Slides fra Webinar om nyt ubalancedesign](https://energinet.dk/el/systemydelser/nyheder-om-systemydelser/2025/02/14/slides-fra-webinar-om-nyt-ubalancedesign/) or [Explanatory-note-nyt-design-for-ubalanceafregning.pdf](https://energinet.dk/regler/el/elmarked/)  (Danish) 

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=now-PT1H](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/ImbalancePrice?start=now-PT1H) is a good approach. Making a request every 10 minutes or so is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
ImbalancePrice.author: Energinet

RegulatingBalancePowerdata.title: Regulating and Balance Power, Overall Data (Discontinued, please read description)
RegulatingBalancePowerdata.description:
This dataset has been Discontinued. Data is available in [Imbalance Price](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/ImbalancePrice) and [mFRR Energy Activation Market](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/MfrrEnergyActivationMarket).

In connection with the go-live of the new imbalance price design, the dataset [Imbalance Price](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/ImbalancePrice) was introduced, replacing [Regulating and Balance Power, Overall Data](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/RegulatingBalancePowerdata). The dataset is in 15-minute resolution and contains all the components relevant to the imbalance price, including the imbalance price, aFRR volume-weighted average price, and mFRR marginal price.

Forecasts_Hour.title: Forecast Wind and Solar Power, Hour Resolution
Forecasts_Hour.description: Forecast of wind and solar power with a resolution of one hour.
Forecasts_Hour.comment:
Solar power forecasts are not updated between 6pm and 6am. Therefore, no 5 Hour forecast exists for Solar power between 11pm and 11am.

1 Hour and 5 Hour forecasts are released up to 15 minutes before the start of the forecast and might be updated until 1 minute before the forecast starts. Within this time frame up to 3 updates can take place. 

The hourly forecast values are calculated from the values in [Forecast Wind and Solar power, 5min](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/Forecasts_5Min).

The following illustrates how the value from 14:00 to 15:00 is calculated:
((Value at 14:00) / 2 + (All values from 14:05 to 14:55) + (Value at 15:00) / 2) / 12.

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=now](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/Forecasts_Hour?start=now) is a good approach. Making a request every few minutes or so is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
Forecasts_Hour.caution:
Data from the Thor offshore wind farm is not included in this dataset.

Due to a technical issue data is missing in the period April 12th-16th 2024 and will not be available.
Forecasts_Hour.author: Energinet

columns.description: A date and time (interval), shown in _UTC time zone_, where the values are valid. 00:00 o’clock is the first hour of a given day interval  00:00 - 00:59 and 01:00 covers the second hour (interval) of the day and so forth. Please note: The naming is based on the length of the interval of the finest grain of the resolution.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00Z. 
That is without the seconds. The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
That is without the "Z".
columns.validationRules: Always full hours, i.e. minutes and seconds are 00
